name: GetNPUsers.py - AS-REP Roasting (Linux)
description: Requests AS-REP tickets for accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled (UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH). The DC encrypts the AS-REP with the account's NT hash — recoverable offline. No credentials needed if using -no-pass with a user list. Hash output in $krb5asrep$23$ format for Hashcat mode 18200.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY AS-REP ROASTING WORKS ===
Kerberos pre-authentication is the default security mechanism: when a user requests
a TGT, they must first prove knowledge of their password by encrypting a timestamp
with their NT hash. This prevents offline cracking of the TGT.

When 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' (UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH) is set
on an account, the DC skips this step and returns an AS-REP encrypted with the
account's NT hash — TO ANYONE WHO ASKS, WITHOUT ANY CREDENTIALS.

This means:
  1. No valid domain credentials required to attack
  2. Request AS-REP for any vulnerable account from any machine
  3. Hash the DC returned is encrypted with the target's password-derived key
  4. Crack offline — no lockout, no noise from repeated attempts

=== WHEN TO USE -no-pass vs WITH CREDS ===
  -no-pass -usersfile users.txt → anonymous/no-auth attack: tries each user,
    DC returns AS-REP if pre-auth is disabled. Requires you have a user list.
  -u user -p pass (authenticated) → can also enumerate which accounts are
    vulnerable AND request their AS-REPs in one shot.

=== OUTPUT TO LOOK FOR ===
  $krb5asrep$23$user@DOMAIN:...  → vulnerable account, hash ready for cracking
  Kerberos SessionError: KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN → user doesn't exist
  Kerberos SessionError: KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED → pre-auth IS enabled (not vulnerable)

=== HASH FORMAT ===
$krb5asrep$23$... → etype 23 (RC4), Hashcat mode 18200
$krb5asrep$18$... → etype 18 (AES256), Hashcat mode 18200 still, but much slower to crack

=== AUTHENTICATED ENUMERATION FIRST ===
If you have creds, find vulnerable accounts first with PowerView:
  Get-DomainUser -PreauthNotRequired | select samaccountname
Then target GetNPUsers.py against those specific accounts.

=== CHAIN POSITION ===
This attack requires NO credentials — ideal for initial access.
Successful crack → password for the account → same spray/lateral movement paths
as any other cracked password. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication).

=== CLOCK SKEW (KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW) ===
Kerberos from Linux fails if your host clock differs from the DC by >5 min:
  'Kerberos SessionError: KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW(Clock skew too great)'.
Fix before impacket/Rubeus runs:
  sudo timedatectl set-ntp off; sudo ntpdate <dc_ip>   # or: sudo rdate -n <dc_ip>

defense.why_it_works: impacket GetNPUsers requests AS-REPs for accounts with pre-auth disabled and outputs crackable hashes - no credentials required if a target list is known.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the DC and a username list (credentials optional).
defense.impact: Crackable AS-REP hashes for accounts with pre-auth disabled.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1558.004] Event 4768 (AS-REQ) with Pre-Authentication Type 0 and RC4 encryption; a request for an account with pre-auth disabled; a honeypot no-preauth account request is malicious.
defense.artifacts: 4768 AS-REQs with pre-auth type 0; the extracted hashes.
defense.prevention: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication (disable only when truly required); enforce 25+ character passwords for any account that must have it off; quarterly review of no-preauth accounts; Defender for Identity detects AS-REP roasting.
defense.evasion: Tools default to RC4 to keep hashes crackable; target a single dormant account to stay quiet.
defense.misconfiguration: The 'Do Not Require Kerberos Preauthentication' checkbox is enabled on the user account (msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes or the UAC flag UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH = 0x400000). This means the KDC issues an AS-REP with the user's session key encrypted by their password hash — without demanding proof of identity first.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Active Directory user account attribute (via ADUC or ADSI Edit)
# 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' = CHECKED
# In PowerShell:
Set-ADAccountControl -Identity svc_backup -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $true

# UAC flag value: 0x400000 (4194304)
# Confirmed with:
Get-ADUser svc_backup -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth
defense.secure_config:
# Enforce Kerberos pre-authentication (the secure default)
# In PowerShell:
Set-ADAccountControl -Identity svc_backup -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# Bulk fix — find and fix all no-preauth accounts:
Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth |
  Set-ADAccountControl -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# GPO path (Kerberos policy):
# Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings >
# Account Policies > Kerberos Policy
# 'Maximum lifetime for user ticket' should be set (forces preauth implicitly)
